meta.titre: Human Reproduction: Gametes, the Menstrual Cycle, Pregnancy and Birth
meta.sous_theme: Hormonal control of the cycle, pregnancy and birth

sections.contenu_markdown: At a health centre in Bafoussam a midwife explains to a young mother why her periods have stopped, why her breasts have changed and how the baby will be born. Every step is controlled by a small set of hormones whose levels rise and fall in a fixed pattern. GCE Advanced Level questions on reproduction ask you to state which hormone does what, which gland releases it, and to read graphs of the menstrual cycle and pregnancy. Learn the pattern once and you can answer most of them.

items: Gametes are haploid cells and fertilisation restores the diploid number of chromosomes.
The testes make sperm and the ovaries make egg cells (ova).
FSH and LH are made by the anterior pituitary; oxytocin is released by the posterior pituitary.
Negative feedback reduces a change; positive feedback increases it.

sections.titre: The menstrual cycle, fertilisation, pregnancy and birth
sections.contenu_markdown:
**Gametes.** Sperm are made in the **seminiferous tubules** of the testis; testosterone is made by the interstitial (Leydig) cells. Sperm pass through the epididymis, the sperm duct and the urethra; the seminal vesicles and prostate gland add fluid containing nutrients (fructose) and alkaline fluid. An egg is released from the ovary at ovulation and enters the oviduct (Fallopian tube).

**Menstrual cycle (about 28 days).**
1. **FSH** from the anterior pituitary stimulates a follicle in the ovary to grow. The follicle secretes **oestrogen**.
2. Oestrogen repairs and thickens the endometrium (uterine lining). When oestrogen reaches a high level, it stimulates (positive feedback) a surge of **LH** and a smaller rise in FSH.
3. The LH surge causes **ovulation** (about day 14).
4. The empty follicle becomes the **corpus luteum** under LH. It secretes **progesterone** (and some oestrogen), which maintains the thick, vascular endometrium and inhibits FSH and LH by negative feedback, so no new follicle develops.
5. If there is no fertilisation, the corpus luteum degenerates, progesterone and oestrogen fall, the endometrium breaks down and **menstruation** occurs. FSH rises again and a new cycle begins.

**Fertilisation** occurs in the oviduct when a sperm head penetrates the egg after the acrosome releases its enzymes; the fertilised egg divides while moving to the uterus. It **implants** in the endometrium about a week after fertilisation.

variantes.quand_utiliser: Questions on hormones in pregnancy or on exchange across the placenta.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
After implantation the embryo secretes **hCG** (human chorionic gonadotrophin), which acts like LH and keeps the corpus luteum secreting progesterone so the endometrium is not shed. Pregnancy tests detect hCG in urine. After about 12 weeks the **placenta** itself secretes oestrogen and progesterone, and the corpus luteum degenerates. Rising progesterone and oestrogen inhibit FSH and LH, so ovulation and menstrual cycles stop during pregnancy.

The placenta allows exchange of oxygen, nutrients, carbon dioxide and urea between maternal and foetal blood by diffusion and active transport; the two blood supplies do not mix.

variantes.quand_utiliser: Questions on oxytocin, prolactin and positive feedback.
variantes.contenu_markdown:
**Progesterone** keeps the uterine muscle quiet during pregnancy. Towards the end, the oestrogen level rises and makes the uterine muscle more sensitive to **oxytocin**. Stretching of the cervix by the foetus sends impulses to the hypothalamus, so the posterior pituitary releases oxytocin; oxytocin causes stronger contractions, which push the head against the cervix and cause more stretching: a **positive feedback** loop that ends with birth.

After birth **prolactin** from the anterior pituitary stimulates milk production, and suckling triggers release of oxytocin, which makes the milk ejection (let-down) reflex contract the milk ducts.

sections.enonce_markdown:
The table gives the relative concentrations (arbitrary units) of four hormones in the blood of a woman on selected days of one menstrual cycle, with menstruation beginning on day 1.

| Day | FSH | LH | Oestrogen | Progesterone |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 5 | 4 | 10 | 1 |
| 7 | 6 | 4 | 30 | 1 |
| 12 | 5 | 6 | 95 | 1 |
| 13 | 9 | 45 | 70 | 2 |
| 14 | 6 | 10 | 50 | 3 |
| 21 | 2 | 3 | 60 | 25 |
| 26 | 3 | 3 | 15 | 4 |

(a) Suggest the day of ovulation. (b) By how many times does LH increase between day 7 and its peak? (c) Explain the cause of the LH peak. (d) Explain why FSH and LH are low on day 21. (e) Explain what causes menstruation to follow.

etapes.action: Find the likely day of ovulation
etapes.justification: Ovulation follows the LH surge by a short time.
etapes.resultat_markdown: LH peaks on **day 13**, so ovulation is expected on about **day 14**.

etapes.justification: Divide the peak value by the value on day 7.
Look at oestrogen just before the peak.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Oestrogen from the developing follicle reaches its highest value (95) on day 12. At this high level oestrogen acts by positive feedback on the anterior pituitary (and hypothalamus), causing the surge of LH.

etapes.action: Explain low FSH and LH on day 21
etapes.justification: Look at progesterone and oestrogen on day 21.
etapes.resultat_markdown: Progesterone (25 units, 25 times its value on day 7) from the corpus luteum and oestrogen are high, and they inhibit the release of FSH and LH by negative feedback, so no new follicles develop.
With no fertilisation the corpus luteum degenerates; progesterone falls from 25 to 4, the endometrium is no longer maintained and breaks down, giving menstruation at about day 28.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The cycle is a chain of feedbacks: FSH, follicle, oestrogen, positive feedback and LH surge, ovulation, corpus luteum, progesterone and negative feedback, then breakdown if there is no pregnancy.

items.erreur_markdown: Ovulation is caused by FSH, which is why FSH is the hormone that peaks just before the egg is released.
items.pourquoi_faux: FSH stimulates the growth of the follicle. The release of the egg is caused by the surge of LH, which is triggered by a high oestrogen level.
items.correction_markdown: FSH → follicle growth → oestrogen; high oestrogen → positive feedback → **LH surge** → ovulation.

items.erreur_markdown: Progesterone makes the uterine muscle more sensitive to oxytocin so that birth can start.
items.pourquoi_faux: Progesterone inhibits contractions of the uterine muscle during pregnancy. Oestrogen increases the sensitivity of the muscle to oxytocin.
items.correction_markdown: Progesterone maintains the pregnancy; **oestrogen** increases the sensitivity of the uterus to **oxytocin**.

items.erreur_markdown: Fertilisation takes place in the uterus.
items.pourquoi_faux: The sperm meet the egg in the oviduct. The uterus is where the embryo implants.
items.correction_markdown: Fertilisation in the **oviduct**; implantation in the **endometrium of the uterus**.

items.erreur_markdown: The mother's blood flows into the foetus's blood in the placenta.
items.pourquoi_faux: The two circulations stay separate; substances cross a thin barrier by diffusion and active transport.
items.correction_markdown: Exchange occurs **across the placental membranes**; the bloods do not mix.

items.erreur_markdown: The menstrual cycle continues during pregnancy.
items.pourquoi_faux: High progesterone and oestrogen from the corpus luteum and then the placenta inhibit FSH and LH, so no follicles mature and no ovulation or menstruation occurs.
items.correction_markdown: Pregnancy is maintained by progesterone, which also stops cycles.

items.enonce_markdown: List in order the structures through which a sperm passes from the seminiferous tubule to the place of fertilisation in the female body, and state the function of the prostate gland.
items.solution_markdown: Seminiferous tubule → **epididymis → sperm duct → urethra → vagina → cervix → uterus → oviduct** (where fertilisation takes place). The prostate gland adds an alkaline fluid with nutrients that helps sperm to swim and protects them in the acidic vagina.

items.enonce_markdown: A woman's last menstrual period began on 12 February 2027. Assume that she ovulated and was fertilised 14 days after the start of that period and that birth occurs 266 days after fertilisation. (a) Calculate the date of fertilisation. (b) Calculate the expected date of birth. (c) How many days after the start of her last period is that, and how many weeks? (d) The placenta takes over hormone secretion at about 12 weeks from the start of the last period. State the date and the hormones involved.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) 12 February 2027 + 14 days = **26 February 2027**.

(b) 26 February 2027 + 266 days = **19 November 2027**.

(c) 14 + 266 = **280 days**, which is 280 / 7 = **40 weeks**.

(d) 12 weeks = 84 days after 12 February 2027, which is **7 May 2027**. The placenta secretes **progesterone and oestrogen**, so the corpus luteum is no longer needed.

items.enonce_markdown: (a) In early pregnancy, assume that the concentration of hCG in a woman's urine is 20 units per dm³ ten days after fertilisation and doubles every two days. Calculate the concentration 18 days and 24 days after fertilisation. (b) Explain why the embryo secretes hCG. (c) Explain how a contraceptive pill containing oestrogen and progesterone prevents ovulation. (d) Say whether each statement is true or false and correct any false one: (i) oxytocin is released from the anterior pituitary; (ii) prolactin causes milk ejection; (iii) progesterone is secreted by the corpus luteum.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) Day 18 is 8 days later: 4 doublings, 20 × 2⁴ = **320 units per dm³**. Day 24 is 14 days later: 7 doublings, 20 × 2⁷ = **2 560 units per dm³**.

(b) hCG acts like LH and maintains the corpus luteum, so progesterone is still made, the endometrium is kept and menstruation does not occur.

(c) The pill keeps the blood level of oestrogen and progesterone high and steady, which inhibits the release of FSH and LH by negative feedback. No follicle matures and there is no LH surge, so there is no ovulation.

(d) (i) **False**: oxytocin is released from the **posterior** pituitary. (ii) **False**: **prolactin** stimulates milk production; **oxytocin** causes milk ejection. (iii) **True**.

items_markdown: Menstrual cycle: FSH grows a follicle, the follicle makes oestrogen, high oestrogen causes the LH surge by positive feedback, and ovulation follows at about day 14.
The corpus luteum makes progesterone, which maintains the endometrium and inhibits FSH and LH; if no pregnancy, it degenerates and menstruation occurs.
Fertilisation takes place in the oviduct and implantation in the uterine lining; hCG from the embryo maintains the corpus luteum.
After about 12 weeks the placenta secretes progesterone and oestrogen; the bloods of mother and foetus do not mix.
At birth, oestrogen makes the uterus sensitive to oxytocin; oxytocin and cervical stretching form a positive feedback loop. Prolactin makes milk, oxytocin ejects it.
